grh_0347f5789c281584a36c.title: Hired Wife
paragraphs: Efficient secretary Kendall Browning secretly loves her boss, cement-company owner Stephen Dexter, but spends every spring watching him fall for another glamorous woman. When a rival company threatens to tie up every asset Stephen owns, his lawyer proposes a temporary marriage so the business can be transferred into a wife's name until the legal danger passes. Stephen wants model Phyllis Walden, but Kendall's attempt to arrange that marriage goes wrong and she ends up becoming Stephen's legal wife herself. Once Kendall controls the company she stops behaving like a compliant secretary, and the resulting battle finally makes Stephen see her as the woman she has always been. Their business marriage becomes real, and Stephen asks her to marry him just before remembering that they already are.

grh_03e0595960bca84ebe3b.title: Alice Bradley Amnesia Victim
paragraphs: A well-dressed young woman arrives at Blair unable to remember her name or past, and Kildare diagnoses psychogenic amnesia rather than brain injury. She is identified as Alice Bradley, but the sight of her wealthy father Albert terrifies her; she later slips out in a nurse's uniform and is found at her mother's grave, where fragments of memory suggest that her mother died on a Swiss lake and that her father murdered her. Kildare and Gillespie learn that Alice recently found her late mother's diary accusing Albert, but Albert explains that his troubled wife went out alone in a canoe while he was away climbing with a group that included her brother George. Using a letter from Uncle George confirming the alibi and the truth about the accident, Kildare breaks through Alice's repression, restores her memory and reconciles her with her innocent father.

grh_03328f384637b313fa5e.title: Such Things Dont Happen
paragraphs: Mrs. Prince opposes her daughter Helen's marriage to recently discharged soldier Johnny Dodd because his family comes from the wrong side of the tracks, while proudly claiming descent from Revolutionary War hero Jonathan Jackson. Dr. Christian argues that Johnny's own service matters more than inherited social standing, but Mrs. Prince refuses to listen. Then Christian encounters Jonathan Jackson himself, apparently returned from the grave. The supposed family hero cheerfully dismantles the legend built around him: he was an ordinary man from an undistinguished family, his famous Revolutionary exploit was greatly exaggerated, and most decisively, he never married and therefore cannot be Mrs. Prince's ancestor at all. Christian brings Jonathan face to face with her. After hearing the truth from the man she has spent years glorifying, Mrs. Prince agrees to Helen and Johnny's marriage and promises them a proper wedding, while Jonathan disappears back into the night as mysteriously as he arrived.

grh_0379ee2952cd4b86ecb8.title: Love Is A Two sided Thing
paragraphs: Newly elected county attorney Grant Newman reopens a manslaughter case against Earl Carlson, unaware that Earl is his wife Eileen's estranged brother. Eileen has hidden her poor background and family from Grant, and the deeper truth is worse: she, not Earl, was driving when an old man was struck, while Earl took the blame to protect her and Grant's political campaign. Dr. Christian finds an eyewitness who proves the death was an unavoidable accident, clearing the driver, but Grant's attempt to dismiss the case makes him look corrupt. Eileen publicly tells the truth to protect her husband from that suspicion, and the crisis forces both spouses to recognize that love and marriage cannot remain one-sided.

grh_030718f22be0cca82bdb.title: Words at War 43-07-17 (04) the Last Days of Sevastopol
paragraphs: A dramatization of Boris Voyetekhov's The Last Days of Sevastopol follows a Soviet correspondent into the besieged city during its final defense against German forces. He witnesses ruined streets, wounded civilians, children involved in reconnaissance, exhausted troops and artillery crews continuing to fight under relentless air and ground attack. grh_03e2e1a5ebeb88ca0c8c.title: The Minstrel Boy
paragraphs: This musical biography follows Irish poet and songwriter Thomas Moore from his early struggle to publish traditional Irish melodies with new lyrics through fame, marriage to singer Bessie and decades of writing. Later Moore tries to create a grand scholarly history of Ireland, only to be crushed when critics find it lifeless compared with his songs. Bessie reminds him that his true gift is the music ordinary people can sing and understand. The story ends with Dubliners honoring Tom and Bessie in the streets while singing the Irish melodies that made him beloved.

grh_039b12f33bb6be02ec0d.title: Words at War 43-10-05 (17) Eighty-Three Days - the Survival of Seaman Izzi
paragraphs: A dramatization of Mark Murphy's 83 Days recounts the true ordeal of Seaman Second Class Basil Izzi after his merchant ship is torpedoed in the South Atlantic. Izzi and a handful of survivors drift for nearly three months on rafts with dwindling food and water, watching companions weaken, go blind and die before being buried at sea. On the eighty-third day a U.S. patrol craft finally recognizes them as survivors and rescues the remaining men, ending one of the war's remarkable stories of endurance at sea.
